lines.text: An AI agent just passed a hidden instruction to one of its tools. It didn't run.
OmniGuard is a security gateway for the Model Context Protocol.
Every tool call passes seven stages, from identity and tool integrity to policy, inspection and audit.
Encoded payloads are decoded before anything inspects them. The rule that fired is named, and explained.
Now a two-step attack. The agent reads a secrets file.
The keys come back masked, and the session is marked sensitive.
Then it tries to send a summary out. The gateway remembers what this session has seen.
Blocking is half the job. Later, you also have to prove what the gateway decided.
Every decision goes to three ledgers. In the third, Merkle roots are written to a contract on-chain.
Play the attacker with root access. Flip a denied record to allowed, then recompute the whole chain.
The table looks clean. The hash chain looks clean. Only the anchored ledger disagrees.
Because the root on-chain cannot be rewritten.
Detection is measured on held-out data. Rules and thresholds were frozen before the test.
On prompt injection, F1 goes from zero point three zero with rules alone to zero point eight four with a pinned classifier.
The model's weights are hash-pinned, and checked before every load.
Forty of forty tamper trials, caught.
Structured calls average under a millisecond, and never touch the model.
It does not catch everything. About a quarter of paraphrased injections still get through, and the report lists them.
OmniGuard-MCP. Every tool call, inspected. Every decision, provable.
